title: CSP Bypass via Missing base-uri Directive
learning_objectives: Understand that script-src (here a per-response nonce) governs WHICH scripts may run, while the base-uri directive governs how RELATIVE script URLs resolve — omitting base-uri leaves a hole even under a strict nonce CSP

See why the CSP must be nonce-based (no 'self'): under 'self' an attacker could inject <script src="/u/<id>/main.js"> directly, so base-uri would be optional; a nonce blocks any injected script and makes the <base> redirect the ONLY path

Exploit a <base href> injection: it repoints the page's OWN nonced relative <script src="main.js"> at attacker content — the nonce lives on the element, so the redirected script loads with a valid nonce
Recognise that ordinary same-origin user content (an upload path) becomes script execution the moment a trusted relative <script src> can be repointed at it via base-uri
Apply the fix: always set base-uri 'none' (or 'self') alongside script-src, and prefer absolute paths / SRI for first-party bundles
flag_hint: The CSP is script-src 'nonce-<random>' (no 'self') with NO base-uri, and the page loads a RELATIVE nonced <script src="main.js" nonce=...> below a reflected ?ref= injection in <head>. A direct <script src="/u/<id>/main.js"> is blocked (no nonce). Upload your JS (POST /upload -> /u/<id>/main.js), then queue /?ref=<base href="/u/<id>/"> — the base repoints the page's OWN nonced main.js to your upload (the nonce rides the element), which runs. Beacon document.cookie, read /oob/received, POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: CSP script-src 'nonce-...' (no 'self') with NO base-uri directive (the flaw)
same-origin upload path /u/<id>/main.js as the base-uri hijack target
inspired_by: The documented base-uri / <base> hijack of relative-path scripts under CSP (Terjanq, Cure53 and the CSP base-uri guidance), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask target that omits base-uri, a same-origin upload path, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
